title: Define per-model SLI taxonomy, error budget enforcement actions, and cross-region failover playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Create a standard, operationally-actionable SLI taxonomy per model, define SLO targets and error-budget enforcement actions, and produce a playbook for cross-region failover including integration points with circuit breakers and load-shedding policies.

Goals:
- Provide a concise set of SLIs (latency, availability, correctness) that are measurable per-model and per-endpoint.
- Define SLO targets associated with customer tiers (free/standard/enterprise) and model classes (small/medium/large).
- Specify error budget consumption rules and automated/manual enforcement actions (rate-limiting, model downgrades, routing to cached responses).
- Produce an operational playbook for multi-region failover including preconditions, automated routing, and human escalation steps.
- Ensure circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding knobs are codified and testable.

Scope:
- Included: API text generation/chat endpoints, embedding endpoints, per-model variants used in hosted and Dedicated.
- Excluded (for now): Private on-prem deploys with custom networking (we'll produce a tailored doc in a follow-up).

Stakeholders: Product (SLA owners), Platform SRE, Runtime team, Console/Observability, Solutions Eng.

Success metrics: clear unambiguous SLIs per-model in monitoring, automated enforcement exercised in chaos test, runbook validated in DR drill, fewer P1 incidents caused by unbounded error budget burn in next quarter.
sli_definitions: request_latency_p50/p95/p99_ms: end-to-end server processing time measured at the API ingress (exclude client-retry delay). Record per-model and per-route. Buckets: p50/p95/p99.
availability_rate: fraction of successful responses (HTTP 200 with schema-compliant payload) over total requests, computed per-model per-region on a 1m and 1h window.

correctness_rate: fraction of responses passing a model-specific validation test (e.g., output schema, presence of required fields, basic hallucination heuristics) measured on a sampled 1% of requests and against synthetic prompt fixtures.
kv_cache_hit_rate: percent of requests served from prefix/KV cache; used for cost-aware SLO adjustments for high-cache workloads.
tail_reject_rate: fraction of requests rejected by per-instance circuit breakers (429/503) due to overload—used to detect excess shedding vs graceful degradation.
slo_targets: Free tier: availability >= 99.0% (30d), latency p95 <= 1200ms for small models, correctness >= 95% on validation fixtures.
Standard tier: availability >= 99.5% (30d), latency p95 <= 700ms for medium models, correctness >= 97%.
Enterprise tier (SLA-backed): availability >= 99.9% (30d), latency p95 <= 250ms on pinned dedicated capacity, correctness >= 98.5% with quarterly regressions testing.
error_budget_policy: Error budget window: rolling 30-day burn calculated per-model per-customer-tier. When budget <= 50% remaining, trigger advisory alerts to owners.

At <= 25% remaining: automated mitigation candidates proposed (lower model size, increase batching, enable degraded model variant); notify product and SRE on-call.
Note: proposals are non-destructive by default and require opt-in for customer-affecting changes unless auto-enforced by policy below.

At <= 10% remaining: pre-authorized automated enforcement may begin for Standard tier (configurable): - enable coarse-grained rate-limiter per API-key to keep 99th percentile latency within SLO - route non-critical traffic to cheaper model variants - enable aggressive prefix cache serving for eligible requests.

At 0% (budget exhausted): Enterprise customers fall back to reserved Dedicated capacity (if configured) or invoke failover plan; all tiers will enter a read-only/limited-serving mode for non-critical endpoints if no capacity: - circuit breakers open aggressively to preserve control-plane stability - console will surface 'Degraded serving' flag and mitigation checklist.
Human escalation: any automated enforcement action must create a tracking incident with root cause hypothesis and owner assignment; review daily until error budget restores.
circuit_breaker_policy:
Per-instance circuit breaker metrics: concurrent_inflight_requests, avg_response_time_window, recent_5xx_rate.
Triggers configured with sliding windows and cool-down periods (default cool-down = 60s).
States: CLOSED (normal), HALF_OPEN (probing small fraction), OPEN (rejecting non-priority traffic).
Priority classification: requests labeled priority=high (webhooks, enterprise web UI) bypass non-critical breakers and have reserved tokens. Low-priority requests are shed first.
Integration: CB events must emit to tracing and monitoring with context (model, region, token, request-path) to allow post-mortem and upstream routing decisions.
Recovery: exponential-probe backoff when in HALF_OPEN, with successful probe threshold of N successes in M attempts configurable per model class.
multi_region_failover_playbook: Preconditions: health aggregation (per-region availability and p95 latency) indicates region R is degraded for >5m and alternative region(s) have capacity headroom >20% sustained for 2m.

Automatic steps (safe mode):
1) Tag read-only or rate-limited for specific model-versions in failing region.
2) Re-route new requests matching eligible policies to healthy region via smart routing layer (respecting data residency and customer config).
3) For sticky sessions, attempt KV-cache warming in target region for high-traffic customers.
4) Notify customers flagged for cross-region failover via console and email for enterprise customers.

Manual escalation (when automatic fails or data residency blocks):
1) SRE on-call to execute guided checklist in Console: promote warm replicas, scale Dedicated pools, or execute customer-scoped throttles.
2) Initiate cross-team war-room for degraded behaved models (runtime, infra, product).
3) Post-failover validation: run smoke queries and correctness fixtures, check telemetry for spike in errors or hallucinations.
Rollback: If correctness regressions detected after region switch, route back and open incident for targeted rollback of model variant or routing rule.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-model SLI overview (30d window), error budget burn chart, circuit-breaker events timeline, region capacity heatmap. Links: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/slo-overview (placeholder).

Alerts: multi-threshold alerts - advisory (budget <=50%), action (<=25%), critical (<=10%). Latency alarms for p99 spikes >2x SLO sustained for 5m. Circuit-breaker alert on >5% global reject rate for 10m.
Sampling and traces: store request traces for 1d by default; increase to 7d for incidents. Export sampled correctness failures to the evals bucket for regression analysis.
testing_and_rollout_plan: Stage 1 (lab): unit tests for SLI calculators and synthetic fixture runner; automate correctness checks.
Stage 2 (canary): enable SLO telemetry for a subset of models and route 5% traffic through SLO-enforcement logic; validate no user-facing regressions for 48h.
Stage 3 (chaos drill): scheduled DR drill to simulate regional outage and validate automatic cross-region failover and error budget enforcements; measure time-to-recover and checklist completion.
Stage 4 (gradual): roll SLO enforcement rules to standard tier, then to free tier with longer cool-downs. Document rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model SLIs are emitted to Prometheus/metrics backend with documented query names and example dashboards.
Error budget policy is codified in a policy repo (policy-as-code) and has unit tests simulating burn scenarios.
Circuit-breaker events are visible in tracing and dashboard and can be toggled via runtime flags.
Cross-region failover executed in a scheduled drill with <5m automation decision time and post-checklist verification.
